units.title: Quadratic variation up to a common stop
units.statement: Evaluate the original finite Itô row at a common bounded stopping time capped by the evaluation time. The dyadic squared-increment sum of this stopped row converges in L¹ to the original square energy accumulated up to that stop, with integrable signed error at every level.
assumptions: One Euclidean Brownian motion under the sample measure μ, relative to the given filtration. The coordinates in a finite index set J come from this same motion.
The sample measure is finite. The horizon T is positive and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions.
Each coordinate input is progressive and product-space square integrable. One [0,T]-valued stopping time τ is shared by all coordinates and satisfies 0 ≤ τ(ω) ≤ T at every sample point.

proof.title: Identify the stopped row at every grid endpoint
proof.text: Use the fixed-time stopping theorem at all endpoints of one finite grid. This identifies the actual stopped row with the completed row of closed stopped integrands almost surely.

proof.title: Identify the stopped energy
proof.text: Squaring the stopped integrand preserves its indicator. Integrate the original coefficient squared on the closed interval ending at τ.

proof.title: Apply the progressive-row theorem
proof.text: Stopping preserves progressive L². Replace the row values and energy at each level by their identified counterparts and use the already proved L¹ limit.

units.boundary: The grid is deterministic. The single common stop is random and is applied to every row evaluation.

units.title: A time primitive has bounded variation
units.statement: The prefix integral of an integrable real time density has finite variation on the closed horizon.
assumptions: The horizon T is nonnegative. The real density b is integrable against nonnegative time measure restricted to [0,T].

proof.title: Control one increment
proof.text: A prefix increment is the integral of b over one time cell. Its absolute value is bounded by the integral of |b| over the same cell.

proof.title: Telescope the bound
proof.text: Sum the bounds on any finite nondecreasing list of times in the horizon. The absolute-density prefixes telescope, and the final prefix is finite.

units.boundary: The Lean conclusion records bounded variation. The proof establishes the displayed quantitative bound, including T=0.

units.title: Weighted mixed products of Brownian increments
units.statement: For distinct coordinates of the same Euclidean Brownian motion, the predictably weighted sum of their simultaneous increment products vanishes in mean square on dyadic grids.
assumptions: One Euclidean Brownian driver and its given filtration.
Distinct coordinates and square-integrable weights measurable at each left endpoint.
One uniform second-moment bound on the weights. T may be zero.

proof.title: Read the mean-square conclusion of the mixed-increment theorem
proof.text: The preceding theorem proves both square integrability at each dyadic level and the asserted vanishing second moment. Select its second conclusion; no extra moment or independence assumption is introduced.

units.boundary: Mean-square control of the literal mixed increment sum for the specified grid weights.

units.title: A Hessian oscillation bound controls the Taylor residual
units.statement: If f is C² at every point of the segment from x to x+v and its Hessian differs there from D²f(x) in operator norm by at most ε, then the Taylor residual has norm at most ε‖v‖².
assumptions: Let E and F be real normed vector spaces. Derivatives are real Fréchet derivatives; D²f(x) is viewed as a continuous bilinear map.
For every t∈[0,1], f is C² at x+tv and ‖D²f(x+tv)−D²f(x)‖≤ε. The constant ε is real; these assumptions imply ε≥0.

proof.title: Differentiate along the segment
proof.text: After subtracting the first derivative and the Hessian at x, the derivative of the first-order error is exactly the Hessian variation applied twice to v.

proof.title: Bound the first-order error
proof.text: The operator-norm bound controls D′. Since D(0)=0, the mean-value inequality on the unit interval bounds D by the same constant.

proof.title: Apply the mean-value inequality a second time
proof.text: The residual along the segment has derivative D and starts at zero. Evaluating its bound at t=1 gives the conclusion.

units.boundary: The constant is an upper bound; no optimal factor of one half is asserted.

units.title: Dyadic predictable Brownian square errors vanish in mean square
units.statement: For the dyadic grids on [0,T], suppose all predictable weights have second moments bounded by one constant C, uniformly over levels and cells. Their compensated weighted square-increment sums tend to zero in mean square.
assumptions: B is a real Brownian motion with the given filtration and measure. The horizon T is any nonnegative real.
At every level n and cell i, the real weight is strongly measurable at time iT/2ⁿ and is in L². A real C satisfies E[aₙ,ᵢ²]≤C for every n,i.

proof.title: Apply the exact finite-grid identity
proof.text: Bound each diagonal weight moment by C and sum the equal cell lengths.

proof.title: Let the mesh tend to zero
proof.text: The upper bound tends to zero and the integrand is nonnegative, so the squeeze theorem gives the limit.

units.boundary: This is mean-square convergence of a centered error, not an almost-sure convergence assertion. It includes T=0.

units.title: Vanishing Taylor residuals on arbitrary fine grids
units.statement: On any compact pseudometric time space, take finite grids whose neighboring time distances vanish uniformly. If the sums of squared state increments converge in measure to a real-valued random variable Q, then the sums of second-order Taylor residuals converge in measure to zero.
assumptions: The sample space Ω carries a finite measure μ. E is a locally compact real normed space with its Borel measurable structure. K⊆E is compact.
f:E→ℝ is C² at every point of K. Each time evaluation of the K-valued process X is measurable. Its paths are continuous on the specified compact time domain for μ-almost every sample.

The time space is compact and pseudometric. Each grid has Nₙ+1 points, and for every δ>0, eventually all neighboring time distances are less than δ. Q:Ω→ℝ is a finite real-valued function. No ordering of the time space is required.

proof.title: Establish measurability of the residual sums
proof.text: The restrictions of f, Df and D²f to K are continuous. Hence the residual as a function of two K-valued endpoints is continuous, and the finite random sums are measurable.

proof.title: Extract a pathwise convergent energy subsequence
proof.text: From any subsequence, convergence in measure provides a further subsequence on which the square-increment sum converges almost everywhere. On each such continuous path it is eventually bounded by C=|Q|+1.

proof.title: Combine small increments with the uniform Taylor estimate
proof.text: Uniform continuity of each path turns the time-mesh condition into small state increments. Apply the compact uniform residual estimate with tolerance ε/(2C). The residual sum is then bounded by ε/2. The subsequence characterization yields convergence in measure.

units.boundary: Convergence of square-increment sums is an explicit input to this reusable lemma; the downstream Itô theorem derives it for its actual process. No rate or almost-sure limit for the full sequence is asserted.
